_meta.source: live capture except where an entry's own _meta says otherwise
_meta.purpose: Every recorded failure mode the FWA data layer must survive offline. Each entry carries the verbatim body, not a paraphrase.
_meta.warning: Several of these errors arrive inside an HTTP 200 (tenderly result cap, ankr auth, multicall unmarshal). A client that branches on HTTP status alone will mis-handle them. Always check for a JSON-RPC 'error' member. Several providers return DIFFERENT messages for the same condition and reuse code -32602 across unrelated conditions, so classification must key on the message text, not the code. And a provider-suggested retry range may be wrong: tenderly's decrements by one block per call.

publicnode_eth_getLogs_refusal.raw_body: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"code":-32602,"message":"Archive requests require a personal token. Get one at: https://www.allnodes.com/publicnode"},"id":1}

error.message: Archive requests require a personal token. Get one at: https://www.allnodes.com/publicnode

publicnode_eth_getLogs_refusal.note: publicnode is the best keyless BATCHER for eth_call but is unusable as a log source. CORRECTION to findings §3, which records this as a flat 'eth_getLogs not supported': the method is in fact served, but ONLY inside geth's ~128-block state-retention window. Anything older is refused by the archive gate with the message below. Since every FWA backfill and every event tail older than ~25 minutes crosses that line, the practical guidance in §3 is correct -- but a client that probes publicnode with a 5-block range at startup will conclude, wrongly, that logs work.
publicnode_eth_getLogs_refusal.expected_client_behaviour: Route ALL log queries to gateway.tenderly.co/public/mainnet, fallback eth.drpc.org. Never capability-probe an endpoint with a narrow recent range and generalise the result.

drpc_block_range_cap.raw_body: {"id":1,"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"message":"ranges over 10000 blocks are not supported on free plan","code":35}}

error.message: ranges over 10000 blocks are not supported on free plan

drpc_block_range_cap.note: eth.drpc.org caps eth_getLogs at 10,000 blocks per request on the free plan. FWA protocol history is ~66,000 blocks, so a naive full backfill fails on its first request. Tenderly has no block cap, which is why it is the primary log source and drpc only the fallback.
drpc_block_range_cap.expected_client_behaviour: Paginate at <= 10,000 blocks whenever the drpc fallback is active. The page size is a property of the endpoint, not of the query -- carry it alongside the URL.

tenderly_result_count_cap.raw_body: {"id":1,"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"code":-32602,"message":"invalid params","data":"Query returned more than 50000 results. Try with this block range [0x185d029, 0x186c47d]."}}

error.data: Query returned more than 50000 results. Try with this block range [0x185d029, 0x186c47d].

tenderly_result_count_cap.note: Tenderly has no BLOCK-range cap but does enforce a 50,000-RESULT cap, and it returns the error inside an HTTP 200. AcquisitionRequested has 58,006 instances all-time, so the one event type that most wants a single-shot backfill is exactly the one that trips this.
tenderly_result_count_cap.expected_client_behaviour: Paginate high-frequency events by block window regardless of endpoint. The error data field names a narrower range to retry -- parse it, or halve the window and retry.

publicnode_archive_refusal.raw_body: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"code":-32602,"message":"Archive requests require a personal token. Get one at: https://www.allnodes.com/publicnode"},"id":1}

error.message: Archive requests require a personal token. Get one at: https://www.allnodes.com/publicnode

publicnode_archive_refusal.note: The same archive gate, hit through eth_call. publicnode serves only ~128 blocks of state. §6.3 requires pinning blockTag across a whole position sweep -- that is fine at head, but reproducing a fixture or backfilling an older block must go to tenderly or drpc.
publicnode_archive_refusal.expected_client_behaviour: Pin blockTag to a block obtained from eth_blockNumber at sweep start and finish the sweep within the retention window. For historical pinned reads use gateway.tenderly.co.

multicall3_invalid_hex_callData.raw_body: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"error":{"code":-32602,"message":"invalid argument 0: json: cannot unmarshal invalid hex string into Go struct field TransactionArgs.data of type hexutil.Bytes"}}

error.message: invalid argument 0: json: cannot unmarshal invalid hex string into Go struct field TransactionArgs.data of type hexutil.Bytes

multicall3_invalid_hex_callData.note: TRAP 4 (§6.5). When hand-encoding Call3(address,bool,bytes), the inner callData must be appended WITHOUT its '0x' prefix. Leaving it on embeds the literal characters '0x' in the middle of the outer data string; the node rejects the entire payload before executing anything. The failure is total and misdirecting -- every call in the batch vanishes and the message blames TransactionArgs.data, not the encoder. Captured against publicnode (go-ethereum), which produces the exact documented wording; tenderly and drpc reject the same payload with vaguer messages, so a client must not string-match on this text.
multicall3_invalid_hex_callData.expected_client_behaviour: Strip the 0x prefix from every inner callData when assembling aggregate3 calldata, and assert the finished data string contains '0x' exactly once, at index 0.

eth_call_gasprice_without_gas_bound.note: NEGATIVE RESULT, recorded deliberately. Findings §7 states that passing gasPrice without also bounding gas makes the node reject the call with 'insufficient funds for gas * price'. That did NOT reproduce here -- tenderly answered successfully. The behaviour is node-specific, so the §7 advice ('pass both gasPrice AND a bounded gas') remains the safe form, but a test must not assert that omitting gas raises.
eth_call_gasprice_without_gas_bound.expected_client_behaviour: Always send BOTH gasPrice and a bounded gas (0x200000) when quoting quoteAcquisitionPrice() / requestFee() / vrfServiceFee(). Do not depend on the error.

publicnode_rate_limit_429.note: publicnode rate-limits under aggressive batching. Findings §3/§11: batch <= 60 elements with ~0.12 s spacing was stable; 150 rapid-fire failed. Multicall3 with <= 500 calls in ONE eth_call is the better shape -- it is a single JSON-RPC element.

drpc_result_cap_too_many_logs.raw_body: {"id":1,"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"message":"query returns too many logs, narrow your filter: 20000","code":-32602}}

error.message: query returns too many logs, narrow your filter: 20000

drpc_result_cap_too_many_logs.note: drpc's RESULT cap, distinct from its 10,000-block RANGE cap. Arrives inside an HTTP 200 with code -32602 -- the same code tenderly uses for its own result cap, so the CODE is not a usable discriminator; the message is. The trailing '20000' is a result count, NOT a block number: a suggested-range parser must not read it as one. No retry range is offered, so the client must halve.
drpc_result_cap_too_many_logs.expected_client_behaviour: Classify as result_cap (shrinkable) and halve the window. Classifying it as a generic rpc error fails the endpoint outright -- this was the live defect.

drpc_result_cap_with_suggested_range.raw_body: {"id":1,"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"message":"query exceeds max results 20000, retry with the range 25583616-25585541","code":-32602}}

error.message: query exceeds max results 20000, retry with the range 25583616-25585541

drpc_result_cap_with_suggested_range.note: The same result cap, other wording, and this one DOES name a retry range -- in DECIMAL, unbracketed, in `message` rather than `data`. Contrast tenderly, which brackets hex in `data`. Both forms must parse. drpc's suggestion is honest: the named range succeeds first try.
drpc_result_cap_with_suggested_range.expected_client_behaviour: Classify as result_cap and retry at the suggested upper bound; it converges in one step instead of ~3 halvings.

drpc_free_plan_timeout.raw_body: {"id":1,"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"message":"Request timeout on the free plan, please upgrade to paid plan","code":30}}

error.message: Request timeout on the free plan, please upgrade to paid plan

drpc_free_plan_timeout.note: INTERMITTENT and load-dependent: the identical request succeeded on a later attempt, returning ~11 MB of logs. Code 30 is drpc-specific. Because it is load- rather than query-shaped, a smaller window genuinely does fix it.
drpc_free_plan_timeout.expected_client_behaviour: Classify as timeout (shrinkable) and retry a smaller window.

_meta.probe: asked for [0x185d029,0x186d1ac] -> suggested 0x186c906; asked for exactly that -> suggested 0x186c905; then 0x186c904; then 0x186c903

tenderly_suggested_range_off_by_one.raw_body: {"id":1,"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"code":-32602,"message":"invalid params","data":"Query returned more than 50000 results. Try with this block range [0x185d029, 0x186c905]."}}

error.data: Query returned more than 50000 results. Try with this block range [0x185d029, 0x186c905].

tenderly_suggested_range_off_by_one.note: THE LIVELOCK. Tenderly's suggested range is not a range that works -- it is the previous request's upper bound MINUS ONE. Following it verbatim decrements one block per round trip and never converges, burning the entire shrink budget. Measured live over four consecutive round trips: 0x186c906 -> 0x186c905 -> 0x186c904 -> 0x186c903.
tenderly_suggested_range_off_by_one.expected_client_behaviour: Treat a suggested range as a HINT and use it only when it shrinks the window materially (>=10%). Otherwise halve. Never follow a suggestion verbatim.
